scans.answer_at_t_val: The three non-logarithmic candidates are f(x)=1/x-1, f(x)=tan((pi/2)(1-x)), and f(x)=Gamma(x)-1. Being decreasing only ensures that raising the probability assigned to an observed token lowers that token's individual loss. It does not ensure that the constrained weighted average sum_i p_i f(q_i) is minimized exactly at Q=P. For that to hold for every P, the first-order condition requires p_i f'(p_i) to be the same constant for all i, hence f'(x) must be proportional to 1/x and f must be a negative logarithm up to scale and an additive constant; monotonic decrease alone does not impose this.
